newsitem.title: USA: O'Leary to ask refiners if they have extra space.
newsitem.headline: O'Leary to ask refiners if they have extra space.

text.p: U.S. Department of Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary said Friday she would ask oil executives whether they had extra capacity in their refineries to produce additional heating oil.
"We really want to probe whether or not the capacity of refineries is full out," O'Leary said to reporters before going into a meeting with 14 top executives from oil and gas companies.
O'Leary called the meeting to discuss heating oil supplies and the outlook for the market this winter amid concern over historically low heating oil stocks.
O'Leary said she was concerned that the low stock situation might not just be an unusual occurrence and might become more common.
"This market for the past six, seven, eight months has been very different from any market I know," O'Leary said.
"I want to get a clear handle on this market that has changed dramatically in the last four to five years," she said.
"We've had this discussion before ... and that indicates to me there's more going on in this market than occasional steep swings (between seasons)," she said.
O'Leary also said she was going to ask the executives to explain how long they expected Europe to be an attractive market for U.S. heating oil exports.
Oil analysts, congressional aides and Energy Department officials do not expect officials in the meeting to announce any concrete action Friday.
